title: Retirement accounts in bankruptcy - federal framework
facts: Federal bankruptcy law provides substantial protection for many tax-qualified retirement funds, subject to statutory requirements.

ERISA-qualified plans such as many 401(k) plans generally receive strong bankruptcy protection, while IRAs are protected under separate Bankruptcy Code provisions and statutory limits or exceptions can apply.
Protection outside bankruptcy and treatment of inherited or nonqualified accounts can differ, so not every account labeled retirement receives identical protection.
A debtor should identify the exact plan or account type before relying on a general retirement-protection rule.
